en.name: Anthony Mary Claret
en.summary: Spanish missionary archbishop and prolific author who founded the Claretian missionary congregation.
en.body: Anthony Mary Claret trained as a weaver before entering the priesthood, and went on to become one of nineteenth-century Spain's most energetic preachers and publishers, founding a religious publishing house and writing over a hundred books and pamphlets to spread Catholic teaching among ordinary readers. In 1849 he founded the Missionary Sons of the Immaculate Heart of Mary, known as the Claretians, dedicated to missionary preaching. Appointed Archbishop of Santiago de Cuba, he worked to reform the Church there amid fierce resistance, surviving an assassination attempt that left a permanent scar. He later served as confessor to the Spanish queen before being forced into exile amid revolution, and died in a monastery in France in 1870.
